assesspathelig.claim: PATh eligibility is tied to an accepted/active or planned/pending NSF award in listed affiliated programs; staff can provide startup credits for workflow prototyping.
assesspathelig.scope: IDSS is not explicitly listed on the checked page. MESA funding alone does not establish eligibility; seek provider/program-officer confirmation before building a course dependency. Absence from the list is not proof of permanent exclusion.

assesspathcredits.title: PATh · research-credit request
assesspathcredits.claim: After prototyping, full PATh credits are requested through the relevant NSF program officer using an award reference and a short technical justification of jobs, cores, memory, runtime and I/O.
assesspathcredits.scope: This is separate from general OSPool education access. No request was sent and no startup or full credits were obtained. An instructor course is not automatically covered by an existing research award.

assessmesaportal.title: MESA portal · existing CyVerse account and quota
assessmesaportal.claim: MESA describes an alternative portal over the user’s CyVerse data, applications and analyses; sign-in reads the existing teams and resource quotas.
assessmesaportal.scope: The portal does not create a duplicate compute allowance. Public documentation is not a signed-in entitlement or load test. Distinguish federally funded IDSS development from underlying state-funded or subscription-funded CyVerse accounts.

assessmesaapps.title: MESA · application/resource selection
assessmesaapps.claim: The portal documents CPU/GPU application variants, launch options and linked Discovery Environment/OSG/Tapis workflows. Its GPU application description names Nvidia A16 nodes.
assessmesaapps.scope: A GPU launch option does not prove permission, quota, class-wide capacity or access to the Jetstream2 A100 flavor modeled separately. Confirm the selected app, runtime, image and data-save behavior.

assessmesasave.title: MESA · save and session lifecycle
assessmesasave.claim: Interactive applications have a time limit that can be extended; files intended for retention belong under ~/data-store. Save & Exit retains outputs; Terminate can discard unsaved session data.
assessmesasave.scope: Rehearse the exact app save/exit/restart/export path. The portal and Data Store are workflow/working-data services, not an independent campus backup or approved archival deposit.

assesscyteach.title: CyVerse · class provisioning
assesscyteach.claim: Instructors can request class/workshop resources, select services, assign organizers and enroll/approve student accounts with institutional addresses. Typical first-Tuesday maintenance should be considered.
assesscyteach.scope: The subscription page requires Pro/Commercial instructor access for workshops and mentions enrollment limits without giving a numeric limit in its current FAQ. Confirm student tiers, class limits and scheduled service windows. One instructor Pro account does not create 80 simultaneous student jobs.

pilotaccessprepare.title: ACCESS · Explore request contents
pilotaccessprepare.claim: Explore requests need a work summary, PI/co-PI CV or résumé PDFs and project metadata. CloudBank’s provider guide additionally asks for course syllabi, enrollments and dates.
pilotaccessprepare.scope: Use the current Explore/provider checklist, not the separate Maximize document requirements. The generated request PDF does not substitute for final syllabus or CV attachments.

pilotuahpcclass.title: UArizona HPC · instruction policy
pilotuahpcclass.claim: Campus HPC documents Puma class groups, shared faculty research/class time allocations, unpredictable queues and instructor-led student help. Consultants can assist instructors but do not provide individual support to all students.
pilotuahpcclass.scope: A documented local alternative, not confirmed account/time quota or reserved classroom capacity. Assess local access honestly before requesting national resources; GPU and deadline priorities are not guaranteed.

pilotuarental.title: UArizona · rental storage rate and lifecycle
pilotuarental.claim: Rental storage lists $47.35/TB/year, billed for the fiscal-year maximum without proration. It is not backed up, though nightly snapshots may allow recent-file recovery. Controlled data is excluded.
pilotuarental.scope: The 3 TB/$142.05 example is capacity rent only, not an approved classroom backup service. Verify eligibility, billing and classification; student work/grades are not authorized for this destination by this report.

pilotuardas.title: UArizona · R-DAS no-cost group storage
pilotuardas.claim: R-DAS provides up to 5 TB per PI group for open research data, with campus/VPN access and PI/group setup. It is separate from HPC-mounted filesystems.
pilotuardas.scope: Potential no-cost location to verify, not a student-by-student entitlement, regulated/private-record destination or independent backup strategy. The site does not request an allocation or approve data placement.

pilotuatier2.title: UArizona · Tier 2 storage billing and restore
pilotuatier2.claim: Tier 2 lists a subsidized first TB of active data, $23/TB/month above that, subsidized transfer, and cold storage/restore stages after inactivity. It excludes controlled data and requires a PI/billing account.
pilotuatier2.scope: The $220.80 six-month comparison assumes 1.6 TB of billed active overage; actual object tiers/charges vary. Cold restores may delay access, so keep a warm independent copy. No classroom data authorization or billing setup is verified.

pilotualibbackup.title: UArizona Libraries · backup and archival boundaries
pilotualibbackup.claim: Libraries distinguishes general working storage from preservation and recommends multiple copies, independent media/location, integrity checks and restore tests. Research storage destinations have data-classification limits.
pilotualibbackup.scope: The pilot needs its own approved data map and retention schedule. Institutional documentation is not evidence that any pilot backup, grade export or repository deposit has succeeded.

pilotinfo521.title: UArizona · INFO 521 course candidate
pilotinfo521.claim: The institutional course description identifies INFO 521: Introduction to Machine Learning as a three-unit course in machine-learning methods and their application.
pilotinfo521.scope: Supports the public course title and conceptual fit only. It does not establish a future offering, enrollment, assigned instructor, syllabus approval or consent to the computing pilot. No private syllabus or intranet content is reproduced.

pilotlis671.title: UArizona · LIS 671 course candidate
pilotlis671.claim: The institutional course description identifies LIS 671: Digital Curation and Digital Preservation as a three-unit course addressing digital-information work in libraries, archives and records management.
pilotlis671.scope: Supports the public course title and conceptual fit only. It does not establish a future offering, enrollment, assigned instructor, syllabus approval or consent to the computing pilot. No private syllabus or intranet content is reproduced.

classroom50.title: Classroom 50: project and license
classroom50.claim: Free, open-source assignment distribution and grading alternative to GitHub Classroom, supported by the Fifty Foundation; project license is GPL-3.0.
classroom50.scope: An independently maintained successor, not a GitHub-operated replacement or an institution-owned hosted service. Documentation fit does not establish classroom adoption.

classroom50model.title: Classroom 50: operation and course data
classroom50model.claim: Hosted static web app or local CLI coordinates GitHub organization teams, repositories, rosters, assignments and scores; grading runs through GitHub Actions.
classroom50model.scope: Course state can live in our institution-controlled GitHub organization. Hosted app stewardship, GitHub service availability and local staffing remain dependencies; ACCESS integration is not demonstrated.

classroom50requirements.title: Classroom 50: prerequisites and education eligibility
classroom50requirements.claim: Requires a GitHub Team or Enterprise organization. Verified teachers can request an education upgrade for their specific organization.
classroom50requirements.scope: Personal teacher verification does not automatically upgrade the organization. Confirm plan, enterprise OAuth policies and actual organization ownership before adoption; no paid upgrade is authorized.

classroom50hosting.title: Classroom 50 web app: hosting and authentication
classroom50hosting.claim: Open-source web app can be self-hosted. Default OAuth exchange and archive proxies use a Fifty Foundation Cloudflare Worker; deployments can configure their own proxy.
classroom50hosting.scope: Self-hosting is an option, not an existing UArizona service. Authentication, proxy traffic, browser token handling, maintenance and recovery need review and available operator time.

classroom50actions.title: Classroom 50: managing Actions cost
classroom50actions.claim: Autograding consumes GitHub Actions resources, with controls needed for workflow usage and spending.
classroom50actions.scope: Actions quotas and charges are separate from Codespaces workspace compute; Classroom 50 adds no Codespaces entitlement. Verify actual billing ownership and spend controls before required use.

changes.name: Heroku
changes.title: Free app hosting and databases end
changes.body: Heroku withdraws free Dynos, Postgres, and Redis plans. Existing free apps and data services face shutdown or deletion.
changes.scope: General-purpose services used in teaching; not an education-only account.

changes.name: GitLab · private teams
changes.title: A private class group no longer fits Free
changes.body: New private Free groups are limited to five users across the namespace. A full cohort needs another plan or a qualifying education program.
changes.scope: Public groups and qualifying Education/Open Source programs are exempt. This restriction rolled out in stages.

changes.name: Replit · new teams
changes.title: No new Teams for Education
changes.body: New education team creation stops. Updates and bug fixes end, leaving instructors unable to use the same setup for a new cohort.
changes.scope: The start of a staged withdrawal; Replit’s broader product continues.

changes.name: Google source hosting
changes.title: A free Git-hosting route closes to newcomers
changes.body: Google Cloud Source Repositories stops accepting new customers. The five-user, 50 GB free route cannot onboard a new eligible organization.
changes.scope: Organizations already using it before the cutoff are unaffected by this access change; no existing-repository shutdown is claimed.

changes.name: Replit · removal
changes.title: Teams for Education is removed
changes.body: The education product closes and its data is deleted after an export period. Teaching materials need a new home.
changes.scope: This is the final stage of the withdrawal announced in 2023.

changes.name: Bitbucket · storage
changes.title: Free workspace storage becomes a bottleneck
changes.body: Bitbucket caps combined repository storage at 1 GB per Free workspace. Over-limit workspaces become read-only; Downloads and Snippets also leave Free.
changes.scope: This is Git storage, not the separate LFS allowance. Paid plans are excluded; special academic-plan terms need checking.

changes.name: Glitch
changes.title: Project hosting shuts down
changes.body: Glitch ends app hosting and user profiles. Live student apps and teaching demonstrations must move.
changes.scope: General-purpose coding/hosting platform. Export access continued through 2025.

changes.name: AWS Free Tier
changes.title: The free-plan window gets shorter
changes.body: The former 12-month limited benefits give way to a credit-based free plan of at most 6 months, ending earlier if credits run out.
changes.scope: General Free Tier used by students; not a blanket change to AWS Educate or Academy. New credits and spending protection also change.

changes.name: CodaLab Competitions
changes.date: End of 2025 · no exact final day established
changes.title: CodaLab passes the torch to Codabench
changes.body: The project reports that CodaLab Competitions and its main servers were phased out at the end of 2025. Codabench is the maintained successor.
changes.scope: Free benchmarking continues on Codabench. Bundles are compatible, but accounts and leaderboards do not transfer automatically. CodaLab Worksheets is separate.

changes.name: GitLab · new groups
changes.title: New Free accounts get fewer course containers
changes.body: New GitLab Free accounts can create only three top-level groups. Repeated course and cohort namespaces need a different organizational plan.
changes.scope: This limits groups, not the number of repositories. Existing accounts are outside this new-account boundary.

changes.name: GitLab · remaining rollout
changes.title: The five-user cap reaches remaining private groups
changes.body: GitLab’s updated notice schedules enforcement on remaining private Free namespaces. Keeping an old class group does not preserve its former allowance.
changes.scope: Final stage of the earlier five-user restriction. Public groups, self-managed Free and qualifying education programs remain exempt.

changes.name: GitHub Classroom
changes.title: GitHub Classroom shuts down
changes.body: The Classroom website, APIs, and related services are decommissioned. New sign-ups had already stopped on May 26.
changes.scope: GitHub accounts, repositories, and organizations remain. Some Classroom metadata is subject to deletion.

changes.name: Colab education offer
changes.title: The education Pro offer quietly closes
changes.body: Google’s FAQ now says free one-year Colab Pro for Education subscriptions are unavailable to new sign-ups. Existing verified users keep their remaining year.
changes.scope: Free Colab still exists. “Quietly” describes the FAQ notice; no exact closure date is established. The original offer was limited.

changes.name: SageMaker Studio Lab
changes.title: Another free notebook door closes
changes.body: AWS no longer accepts new Studio Lab customers and plans no new features. Existing users can continue.
changes.scope: A new-access restriction, not a full service shutdown. The current provider notice does not state an effective date.

degree_options.name: BS Information Science
degree_options.good: Python / R / SQL labs, small-data models and short GPU experiments. Browser prototypes for the immersive emphasis.
degree_options.limit: Large training, concurrent GPUs, high-memory data or immersive hardware are required.
degree_options.handoff: ACCESS CPU / GPU labs; NAIRR Classroom for AI courses; campus XR hardware.
degree_options.supplement: Codabench / Kaggle competitions for small prediction benchmarks; Binder for short CPU labs; CodeGrade for ≤50-student coding labs.

degree_options.name: MS Data Science
degree_options.good: Reproducible notebooks, tabular ML, sampled datasets and checkpointed deep-learning labs.
degree_options.limit: Data exceeds RAM / storage, models exceed available VRAM, or jobs need long / distributed training.
degree_options.handoff: ACCESS for larger data and scheduled capacity; NAIRR Classroom for AI instruction.
degree_options.supplement: Codabench / Kaggle competitions for model evaluation; Lightning for credit-bounded pilots; ZeroGPU for brief inference demos.

degree_options.name: MS Information Science
degree_options.good: ML subplan: notebook experiments. Human-Centered Computing: web prototypes and small public-data studies.
degree_options.limit: Training or deployment must persist; studies need controlled data, full desktops or specialized devices.
degree_options.handoff: Managed ACCESS environments; NAIRR Classroom where the course teaches AI.
degree_options.supplement: Codabench / Kaggle competitions for ML; ZeroGPU for HCC model demos; CodeGrade for small programming labs.

degree_options.name: BA Emerging Technologies in Society
degree_options.good: Small public-text / network analyses, web development, digital storytelling and public portfolios.
degree_options.limit: Live app backends, licensed social-media data, private participant records or large corpora are required.
degree_options.handoff: ACCESS for larger analysis or managed servers; retain institution-approved study tools.
degree_options.supplement: Binder for short public-text analysis; CodeGrade for small coding labs; Kaggle hackathons for judged public-data projects.

degree_options.name: BA Game Design
degree_options.good: Branching narratives, rules and interaction prototypes, browser playtesting and published HTML games.
degree_options.limit: A project needs a full 3D engine, large assets, persistent multiplayer servers or VR headsets.
degree_options.handoff: Campus engine / device labs; evaluate allocated GPU desktops and server support.
degree_options.supplement: Kaggle hackathons for judged prototypes; CodeGrade for small scripting labs. Neither supplies a 3D engine, XR device or game server.

degree_options.name: BS Game Development
degree_options.good: Game logic, headless tests, small JavaScript games and browser-playable prototypes.
degree_options.limit: Unity / Unreal desktop workflows, heavy 3D builds, rendering, VR or persistent multiplayer are required.
degree_options.handoff: Campus game / XR labs; ACCESS servers or GPU desktops after software and license checks.
degree_options.supplement: CodeGrade for small code/test labs; Codabench only for bounded custom-scored agents with supplied workers. Heavy engine builds remain elsewhere.

degree_options.name: BA Information Science & Arts
degree_options.good: Creative coding, interactive graphics, audio-visual sketches and web-based UX prototypes.
degree_options.limit: Work needs high-end rendering, large media, installed creative software, XR devices or physical installations.
degree_options.handoff: Campus media / XR labs; allocated GPU or remote desktops where appropriate.
degree_options.supplement: ZeroGPU for brief AI behavior demos; Kaggle hackathons for judged creative projects. Rendering/XR work still needs appropriate hardware.

degree_options.name: MA Library & Information Science
degree_options.good: Metadata cleaning, Python / R / SQL exercises, small text collections and static digital exhibits.
degree_options.limit: A repository / ILS must run continuously, preservation storage must endure, or collections need access controls.
degree_options.handoff: Managed ACCESS teaching servers plus library systems; NAIRR Classroom for AI coursework.
degree_options.supplement: Binder for metadata/text workshops; Codabench / Kaggle competitions for retrieval or classification metrics. Archives/ILS require durable systems.

degree_options.name: PhD Information
degree_options.good: Methods coursework, pilot analyses, reproducible examples and small model feasibility studies.
degree_options.limit: Dissertation work needs sustained GPU time, large-scale simulation, controlled data or durable services.
degree_options.handoff: ACCESS / appropriate NAIRR research requests for research; Classroom only for eligible instruction.
degree_options.supplement: Codabench / EvalAI for research evaluation; Binder for reproducible methods; Lightning for small pilots. Sustained research compute requires an allocation.

codespaces.name: GitHub Codespaces
codespaces.quota: 60 h / month on 2 cores; 90 h for verified students.
codespaces.detail: 120 / 180 core-hours; 15 / 20 GB-month storage. Personal-account quotas; larger machines use hours faster. No generally available GPU.

kaggle.name: Kaggle Notebooks
kaggle.quota: Weekly GPU quota varies. No reserved classroom seats.
kaggle.detail: Short, checkpointed notebook jobs; check the account quota and session timer. GPU memory and saved disk constrain models and data.

pages.name: GitHub Pages
pages.quota: Static sites up to 1 GB; public sharing on the free tier.
pages.detail: HTML / CSS / JavaScript hosting. Code executes on the viewer’s device; no application server, database or cloud GPU.

p5.name: p5.js Web Editor
p5.quota: Free creative coding; uses the student’s device.
p5.detail: Browser graphics and audio; device performance still matters. This is not a remote rendering workstation or allocated GPU.

twine.name: Twine
twine.quota: Free narrative authoring; export portable HTML.
twine.detail: Runs in the browser or a local app. Keep backups of story files; this is not a cloud engine workstation.

repository_plan.title: 1 · Keep a viable free route
repository_plan.body: Use GitHub Free for ordinary Git hosting now. Assess an institution-sponsored GitLab for Education application for private class teams and additional features; annual renewal and use restrictions still apply. Classroom 50 is a workable assignment-management successor, externally maintained by the Fifty Foundation. Keep course repositories/configuration in an institution-controlled GitHub organization; verify Team/Enterprise education eligibility, retain exports and rehearse an alternate submission path. It adds no Codespaces compute allocation.
repository_plan.owner: Instructor lead + college IT · before the next course

repository_plan.title: 2 · Establish campus ownership
repository_plan.body: Inventory course repos, sizes, LFS, issues, wikis, artifacts and grading links. Give each course a responsible owner and successor. Keep submissions private; do not make student work public to escape a quota.

repository_plan.title: 3 · Pilot a managed fallback
repository_plan.body: Evaluate a supported campus Git service first. If none fits, pilot Forgejo or self-managed GitLab on an institution-managed host with authentication, private projects, quotas and isolated grading runners. Budget staff, durable storage and recovery separately from compute awards.

repository_plan.title: 4 · Preserve more than Git
repository_plan.body: Take versioned nightly Git and LFS backups to independent storage; export issues, wikis, release files and course assessment links through supported paths. Define retention, access and deletion rules. A live mirror can copy deletions and cannot replace a separate backup.
repository_plan.owner: Named service operator · nightly; alert on failures

repository_plan.title: 5 · Prove recovery, then scale
repository_plan.body: Before teaching, restore a private sample course on a second host and confirm history, LFS, permissions and grading links. Proposed pilot targets: at most 24 hours of data loss and recovery within one business day. Validate these targets before promising them.
repository_plan.owner: Operator + instructor · pre-term and after major changes

repository_plan.title: 6 · Close the teaching cycle
repository_plan.body: Give students portable code exports, retain institutional assessment records under approved policy, and archive releasable research code/data with Libraries/ReDATA when appropriate. Review storage, restores, licenses and allocation renewal before the next cohort.

library_repository_findings.title: OSF Projects
library_repository_findings.finding: New project creation stops; existing projects become read-only. Active research collaboration and file-management exercises need a new workspace.
library_repository_findings.boundary: Public records remain; preregistration and community preprint services continue. Both effective dates are upcoming as of this audit.

library_repository_findings.title: Generalist OSF Preprints
library_repository_findings.finding: New submissions to the generalist server stopped, narrowing a scholarly-communication teaching route.
library_repository_findings.boundary: Existing papers and revisions remain; community-led preprint servers are excluded.

library_repository_findings.title: Dryad
library_repository_findings.finding: Size-based charges make sponsorship and dataset size material to publishing costs; partner coverage generally stops at 10 GB.
library_repository_findings.boundary: Dryad was not universally free before this change. Sponsorship and waivers can cover eligible deposits; no campus agreement was verified.

library_repository_findings.title: Google education working storage
library_repository_findings.finding: Education storage moved to a baseline institutional pool of 100 TB across users and accounts.
library_repository_findings.boundary: A shared Drive quota affects preparing deposits and collaboration, not the preservation status of an institutional repository. Campus contract capacity may differ.

library_repository_findings.title: Microsoft education working storage
library_repository_findings.finding: Free A1 OneDrive users face a 100 GB cap; institutional pooled storage adds a separate constraint.
library_repository_findings.boundary: Paid-license additions and contract-renewal timing matter. This is not a 100 GB cap on every UArizona account.

library_repository_findings.title: Figshare and Zenodo
library_repository_findings.finding: Figshare offers 20 GB private storage; Zenodo provides a default 50 GB per published record with additional quota options.
library_repository_findings.boundary: Useful continuing publication routes. Current limits alone cannot establish a five-year reduction.

library_repository_findings.title: Omeka digital collections
library_repository_findings.finding: One free hosted site and 500 MB fit a small metadata/exhibition assignment. Large scans and audiovisual collections need another storage plan.
library_repository_findings.boundary: No recent free-plan reduction was verified. Self-hosting moves infrastructure and support responsibility to the institution.

library_repository_findings.title: Institutional preservation systems
library_repository_findings.finding: DSpace software is free; managed repository and preservation services fund hosting, maintenance and support through subscriptions.
library_repository_findings.boundary: A sustainability dependency, not proof of a recent account cut. Free software and funded preservation are separate commitments.

library_repository_findings.title: UArizona ReDATA
library_repository_findings.finding: Libraries reports intermittent errors and temporary automated-download restrictions due to high-volume traffic.
library_repository_findings.boundary: This is not a closure, account reduction or breach. ReDATA remains a curated public research repository with DOIs.

library_repository_findings.title: UArizona Campus Repository
library_repository_findings.finding: Free-to-campus public deposit of suitable publications, reports, theses and other scholarly materials remains available.
library_repository_findings.boundary: Coordinate collections and content suitability with Libraries; private submissions and live apps require other services.

hosting_database_findings.title: Heroku apps + Postgres + Redis
hosting_database_findings.finding: Free Dynos, Postgres and Redis plans ended; free databases faced deletion.
hosting_database_findings.boundary: General-purpose teaching infrastructure. Hosting and databases are one provider event; later student credits require separate verification.

hosting_database_findings.title: Railway recurring credits
hosting_database_findings.status: Allowance withdrawn; smaller free plan now
hosting_database_findings.finding: The original recurring $5 monthly Starter allowance became a one-time trial. Railway now offers a $1 monthly Free allowance.
hosting_database_findings.boundary: Avoid the stale claim that Railway has no free tier today. Current credits still do not guarantee a semester of hosting or databases.

hosting_database_findings.title: PlanetScale Hobby
hosting_database_findings.finding: The free Hobby plan retired and remaining databases were put to sleep, with a short export wake-up route.
hosting_database_findings.boundary: PlanetScale continues as a paid service; this is not the closure of all its databases.

hosting_database_findings.title: Cyclic app hosting
hosting_database_findings.date: Free turn-off began May 10; all usage May 31, 2024
hosting_database_findings.finding: A free full-stack app-hosting route disappeared when Cyclic shut down.
hosting_database_findings.boundary: Dates describe the provider’s announced staged turn-off; individual deployment or deletion outcomes were not audited.

hosting_database_findings.title: Render free PostgreSQL
hosting_database_findings.finding: Free database lifetime shortened by two thirds. The 14-day upgrade grace period follows expiry, then data is deleted.
hosting_database_findings.boundary: Legacy databases retained their original expiry. Free web hosting survives; a free 30-day database is not a semester solution.

hosting_database_findings.title: Fly.io new organizations
hosting_database_findings.date: Plans discontinued October 7, 2024; current policy checked October 10, 2026
hosting_database_findings.finding: Old eligible organizations retain free allowances; new organizations receive a short trial and pay for continued billable resources.
hosting_database_findings.boundary: Do not portray October 2024 as the first removal of every free Hobby signup. Earlier plan changes existed; the current new-account trial lasts at most two runtime hours or seven days.

hosting_database_findings.title: ElephantSQL managed Postgres
hosting_database_findings.finding: After end of life and a staged brownout, the service terminated and its timeline specified deletion of all data.
hosting_database_findings.boundary: The final data-deletion date is February 28, not January 27. Both free and paid customers were affected.

hosting_database_findings.title: Fauna managed database
hosting_database_findings.finding: The database service shut down; applications needed a new endpoint and exported data.
hosting_database_findings.boundary: A whole-service loss affecting free and paid customers, confirmed by the provider status page.

hosting_database_findings.title: Glitch app hosting
hosting_database_findings.finding: Project hosting and user profiles ended. Live student apps and demos needed migration.
hosting_database_findings.boundary: Code downloads continued through the end of 2025; this did not preserve execution of the apps.

hosting_database_findings.title: Netlify Free
hosting_database_findings.finding: New Free accounts share 300 monthly credits across deploys, compute and traffic; all web projects pause when credits are exhausted.
hosting_database_findings.boundary: Free hosting remains. Eligible older accounts can retain legacy plans. The new model is not an equivalent capacity cut for every workload.

hosting_database_findings.title: Firebase Cloud Storage
hosting_database_findings.finding: Access requires a Blaze project linked to Cloud Billing, even when usage fits a no-cost allowance.
hosting_database_findings.boundary: Object storage, not a shutdown of Firebase Hosting or Firestore. Existing data remains inaccessible until upgrade; overages can cost money.

hosting_database_options.fit: Static course sites, public exhibits, metadata presentations and browser apps.
hosting_database_options.limits: Pages does not run a persistent backend. GitHub published sites are limited to 1 GB; Cloudflare has 20,000 files/site and 25 MiB/asset. Public outputs need appropriate rights.

hosting_database_options.fit: Lightweight web APIs and small SQLite-style CRUD exercises.
hosting_database_options.limits: Workers: 100,000 requests/day and 10 ms CPU/invocation. D1: ten databases/account, 500 MB each, 5 GB total, five million rows read/day and 100,000 written/day. Not PostgreSQL or a long-running analysis server.

hosting_database_options.fit: Small PostgreSQL exercises and intermittent student app backends.
hosting_database_options.limits: 100 CU-hours/project/month; 1 GB/project and 20 GB/account total. Scales to zero after five idle minutes. Short recovery history needs independent exports; benchmark full-class concurrency.
Two active projects; 500 MB database/project and 1 GB file storage. Pauses after a week idle. Export database and uploaded files separately; free managed-backup guarantees must not be assumed.

hosting_database_options.fit: Small Python/Node web demos when cold starts are acceptable.
hosting_database_options.limits: Sleeps after 15 minutes idle; 750 service-hours shared per workspace. Ephemeral filesystem. Free Postgres expires in 30 days; use another durable database for a semester project.

hosting_database_options.fit: Small document-database, metadata and aggregation exercises.
hosting_database_options.limits: 0.5 GB includes data and indexes; one Free cluster/project. No managed backups or sharding; pauses after 30 days without connections. Export and rehearse manual restore.

hosting_database_options.fit: Small static and serverless demos with measured credit consumption.
hosting_database_options.limits: 300 credits/month; quota exhaustion pauses all web projects. Legacy account terms differ. Deploy/traffic/compute compete for the same allowance.

hosting_database_options.fit: Eligible personal, non-commercial student web demos.
hosting_database_options.limits: Personal-use terms and no paid team collaboration. Execution and usage quotas apply; a college-wide service cannot be assumed eligible.

hosting_database_options.fit: Very small metered deployments or an introductory deployment exercise.
hosting_database_options.limits: $1 recurring monthly credit is useful but insufficient to promise a full semester or always-on database. Distinguish this from the $5 one-time trial and paid Hobby.

service_continuity_plan.title: Inventory the whole course stack
service_continuity_plan.body: For two pilot courses, map compute, live app, database, object files, Git, and archival deposits. Record each owner, account, region, quota, expiry and course requirement. Distinguish public teaching examples from private submissions and research materials.
service_continuity_plan.owner: Instructor + college IT + Libraries · 12–10 weeks before term

service_continuity_plan.title: Choose a bounded free route and a funded fallback
service_continuity_plan.body: Use static hosting where no backend is needed; Neon for small Postgres coursework, Workers/D1 for lightweight SQLite-style apps, or Supabase when integrated auth is part of the exercise. Provision through supported institutional services when available. For persistent multi-user courses, fund managed app/database hosting or an IT-supported environment through the assessment and export period.
service_continuity_plan.owner: College IT + course lead · 10–8 weeks before term

service_continuity_plan.title: Separate compute awards from service operations
service_continuity_plan.body: Request reviewed ACCESS capacity and eligible NAIRR Classroom pilots for instruction and analysis. Separately commit the budget and operator for databases, application availability, durable object storage, identity, backups and renewal. Do not assume a research allocation supports permanent public hosting or preservation; check the awarded resource’s rules.
service_continuity_plan.owner: College leadership + IT + allocation lead · before committing the course

service_continuity_plan.title: Make the course portable and recoverable
service_continuity_plan.body: Keep versioned app source, schema migrations, dependency definitions and synthetic seed data. Export the database and uploaded files independently to institution-approved storage; include metadata, licenses, checksums and necessary access configuration. Protect credentials and define retention with the appropriate institutional owners. A Git mirror or provider snapshot alone does not preserve this whole stack.
service_continuity_plan.owner: Named service operator · automated backups with failure alerts

service_continuity_plan.title: Rehearse real class load and a second-host restore
service_continuity_plan.body: Test simultaneous class use, cold starts, deployment/egress/query quotas, inactivity and expiration handling. Restore an app, database and sample file set onto a second host; verify private access, schema, queries and grading links. Proposed pilot recovery targets remain at most 24 hours of data loss and one business day to restore; measure them before promising them.
service_continuity_plan.owner: Operator + instructor · 4–2 weeks before term and after major changes

service_continuity_plan.title: Close and preserve the course deliberately
service_continuity_plan.body: Offer portable student exports; retain assessment records under approved policy. Coordinate suitable public scholarly deposits with Campus Repository, ReDATA or a disciplinary repository, including metadata and persistent identifiers. Budget stewardship beyond the award period. Recheck vendor terms and test recovery before the next cohort; move active OSF Projects before the announced freeze.
service_continuity_plan.owner: Instructor + Libraries + IT · end of term and annual review

Current quotas do not establish historical reductions.
Dryad changed fees; this is not a universal free-to-paid conversion.

ACCESS/NAIRR capacity is proposed, conditional and time limited; durable services require separate operations.

The Cyclic provider URL fails certificate verification; the same notice is linked on its author’s live site.

classroom_resource_options.name: Classroom 50
classroom_resource_options.access: Free, open-source assignment workflow · evaluate before adoption
classroom_resource_options.fit: Workable successor for GitHub Classroom assignment distribution, repositories, submissions, feedback and grading.
classroom_resource_options.limits: Fifty Foundation project and hosted app are not ours. Requires a Team/Enterprise organization; check education eligibility. No additional Codespaces compute; Actions grading has separate quotas. ACCESS remains the CPU/GPU classroom route.

classroom_resource_options.name: Codabench
classroom_resource_options.access: Free benchmark hosting; compute depends on queue
classroom_resource_options.fit: Prediction scoring, reproducible code benchmarks and common test environments.
classroom_resource_options.limits: Shared CPU scoring jobs ≤20 minutes. Organizers supply queues for code submissions and all GPU workers; no GPU notebook or whole-class reservation.

classroom_resource_options.name: Kaggle Community Competitions
classroom_resource_options.fit: Prediction-file competitions with live leaderboards; judged hackathons for open-ended projects.
classroom_resource_options.limits: Training happens elsewhere or in separately limited notebooks. Restricted-email competitions disable notebooks by default; community hosting has no hands-on support.

classroom_resource_options.name: CodeGrade
classroom_resource_options.fit: Programming labs with browser editing, immediate autograding and instructor feedback.
classroom_resource_options.limits: Check free-plan execution/LMS limits and roster scope. No verified free GPU entitlement or campus deployment; grading records need approved retention.

classroom_resource_options.name: ChaGrade
classroom_resource_options.access: Adjacent project; current free entitlement unverified
classroom_resource_options.fit: Challenge-linked individual/team homework and instructor grading beyond leaderboard scores.
classroom_resource_options.limits: Live page labels version 0.1 / Work In Progress. Support, quotas and current Codabench integration need verification; not a ready college-wide baseline.

classroom_resource_options.name: EvalAI
classroom_resource_options.fit: Custom prediction/code evaluation and organizer-controlled remote workers.
classroom_resource_options.limits: Hosted plans $125–850/month; remote evaluation $100/month plus own compute. Self-hosting requires funded staff, infrastructure and storage. No verified hosted free tier.

classroom_resource_options.name: CodaLab Competitions
classroom_resource_options.access: Retired at end of 2025; successor available
classroom_resource_options.fit: Historical challenge service; migrate compatible competition bundles to Codabench.
classroom_resource_options.limits: New account required; leaderboards do not transfer automatically. Preserve submissions/results separately. Separate CodaLab Worksheets is not covered.

classroom_resource_options.name: GitHub Codespaces
classroom_resource_options.fit: Reproducible Python/R/SQL labs, small analysis and code development before submission.
classroom_resource_options.limits: 60 two-core hours/month, or 90 for verified students; storage quota and machine sizes matter. No generally available GPU; not continuous application hosting.

classroom_resource_options.name: Kaggle Notebooks
classroom_resource_options.fit: Checkpointed small-model GPU experiments and training for a competition.
classroom_resource_options.limits: Check each account’s GPU quota, available hardware, session timer and saved disk. No reserved class seats or distributed/long-running training promise.

classroom_resource_options.name: Free Google Colab
classroom_resource_options.fit: Short shared notebooks, CPU analysis and opportunistic accelerator exercises.
classroom_resource_options.limits: GPU access and resource/session limits fluctuate. Free Colab is separate from the closed new-signup education Pro offer; never promise class GPU availability.

classroom_resource_options.name: mybinder.org
classroom_resource_options.fit: Small Python/R notebooks launched from a reproducible repository, including metadata/text workshops.
classroom_resource_options.limits: 1–2 GB RAM; ten-minute idle shutdown; aims for ≤6 hours or one CPU-hour; 100 concurrent sessions per repo. Download work; no GPU or persistent workspace promise.

classroom_resource_options.name: Lightning AI Studio
classroom_resource_options.access: Free CPU studio; conditional introductory GPU credits
classroom_resource_options.fit: Browser development, small pilot experiments and checkpointed training within actual credit balance.
classroom_resource_options.limits: Four-hour free restart boundary; five credits at signup, 25 more with a card, not a fixed monthly grant. Ten GB free storage; rates/machine size and stopping/billing behavior need checking.

classroom_resource_options.name: Hugging Face ZeroGPU / Spaces
classroom_resource_options.access: Five GPU minutes/day for signed-in Free users
classroom_resource_options.fit: Short Gradio inference demos and model-behavior comparisons; static exhibits on free Static Spaces.
classroom_resource_options.limits: Two own ZeroGPU Spaces only for eligible personal accounts ≥30 days old. Shared queues and Gradio constraints; organization hosting paid. Ordinary compute-backed Space creation also needs a paid plan.

classroom_resource_options.name: cuda.live
classroom_resource_options.fit: Tiny CUDA kernel/compiler demonstrations independent of the Codabench workflow.
classroom_resource_options.limits: Advertised T4 16 GB, five runs per 15 minutes; per-execution allowance is not GPU-hours. Existing October 8 verification, no reserved class capacity.

classroom_resource_extension.method: Exa discovery, primary documents, direct live HTML and rendered Lightning pricing. Requested slots are discovery, not independently validated source counts.
source_access_notes: Codabench homepage extraction from Exa and web was unrelated text; direct live HTML confirmed real content and the 20-minute queue cap.

Lightning current live rendered FAQ specifies five signup credits plus 25 for adding a card; older monthly-credit claims were not adopted. Billing docs and pricing differ on machine size; verify actual account.
ChaGrade is retained as an adjacent workflow with unverified entitlement/readiness, not counted as guaranteed free capacity.
classroom_resource_extension.proposal: Pilot a permitted Codabench evaluation queue backed by reviewed ACCESS capacity; isolated workers, scheduling, operations, storage, backups and grade exports remain separate requirements.

federal_platform_map.name: ACCESS
federal_platform_map.funding: NSF-funded coordination + separately funded resource providers
federal_platform_map.route: ACCESS project request; exchange credits for provider resources
federal_platform_map.fit: Broad CPU/GPU research and instruction; resource discovery and support.
federal_platform_map.boundary: Provider quotas, scheduling, allocation term and software vary. Counts overlap with participating resource providers.

federal_platform_map.name: OSG Open Science Pool (OSPool)
federal_platform_map.route: Documented guest education notebook or facilitated full event accounts
federal_platform_map.fit: Independent text/image analyses, parameter sweeps, model evaluation and many short CPU/GPU jobs.
federal_platform_map.boundary: Guest four-hour timeout/files may be lost; full accounts usually end shortly after event. Interruptible fair share; complete/checkpoint jobs within 20 hours. No sensitive/proprietary data or classroom GPU reservation.

federal_platform_map.name: PATh Facility
federal_platform_map.route: Consult PATh; NSF-funded project startup/credit process
federal_platform_map.fit: Dedicated throughput research jobs when the affiliated NSF program and credits are confirmed.
federal_platform_map.boundary: IDSS is not explicitly listed in the published affiliated-program policy. MESA funding alone does not establish eligibility or course authorization; confirm with PATh/NSF. Separate from OSPool education access.

federal_platform_map.name: NRP / Nautilus
federal_platform_map.route: Institutional onboarding; hosted JupyterHub, API or project namespace
federal_platform_map.fit: Hosted teaching notebooks, GPUs, open-weight model APIs and containerized services.
federal_platform_map.boundary: Hosted hub starts with 5 GB homes; larger storage, class/GPU quota and hub-specific exceptions need approval. Ordinary-pod six-hour rules do not establish every hub limit. Not archival storage; idle volumes may be purged.

federal_platform_map.name: Jetstream2
federal_platform_map.route: ACCESS allocation, course images and student/project access
federal_platform_map.fit: Notebooks, RStudio, desktops, web/database teaching servers and vGPU environments.
federal_platform_map.boundary: Always-on VM accounting, separate GPU exchange, concurrent quota and extra storage need approval. Independent backups required. Expiry/overdraw disables access and can destroy unresolved resources after thirty days.

federal_platform_map.name: NAIRR / NAIRR Classroom
federal_platform_map.route: Appropriate researcher or Classroom request
federal_platform_map.fit: AI coursework, GPUs, model/data/tools and selected managed environments.
federal_platform_map.boundary: US-based class eligibility and approved resources; instructor/TA support expected. Research and Classroom requests differ; partner offerings are not all federally purchased.

federal_platform_map.name: CloudBank / CloudBank Classroom
federal_platform_map.kind: Commercial-cloud broker and managed teaching platform
federal_platform_map.route: General ACCESS Explore Classroom route; separate NAIRR Classroom route for AI coursework
federal_platform_map.fit: Managed Python/R/C++ browser environments with login and student storage.
federal_platform_map.boundary: Managed CPU per-student limits/capacity need confirmation. Current registry says fall 2026 GPU pilot is at capacity; requests considered in 2027, not guaranteed. Renewal terms need reconciliation with education-period policy.

federal_platform_map.name: Chameleon / CHI@Edge
federal_platform_map.route: Eligible PI project; allocation and resource lease
federal_platform_map.fit: Systems/MLOps, edge/IoT, bare-metal experiments, specialized GPU/FPGA hardware.
federal_platform_map.boundary: Experiment purpose, SU budget and short hardware leases. No unrestricted production hosting; student membership normally follows PI approval.

federal_platform_map.name: CloudLab
federal_platform_map.route: Approved project with planned class reservations
federal_platform_map.fit: Distributed systems, reproducible root-access labs and networked application experiments.
federal_platform_map.boundary: Use only while actively experimenting; node data disappears at termination. Reserve for deadline bursts and export work.

federal_platform_map.name: FABRIC
federal_platform_map.route: Project and experimental resource slices
federal_platform_map.fit: Distributed AI, edge workloads, streaming/data movement and instrument-to-compute experiments.
federal_platform_map.boundary: Experiment should need the network/testbed capabilities; not a stand-alone generic GPU account or production campus server.

federal_platform_map.name: NSF NCAR Derecho / analysis resources
federal_platform_map.route: Classroom/workshop or qualifying research allocation
federal_platform_map.fit: Earth-system, environmental and geospatial data/AI instruction with consulting.
federal_platform_map.boundary: Earth-system mission fit; setup lead time, accounts, dates and reservations required. Separate grant not required for eligible classes.

federal_platform_map.name: DOE NERSC / ALCF / OLCF
federal_platform_map.route: ALCC, INCITE or facility-specific merit request
federal_platform_map.fit: Large mission-aligned scientific simulation, data analysis and AI research.
federal_platform_map.boundary: ALCC does not require DOE sponsorship, but merit/mission/scaling requirements apply. Not the default for everyday college labs.

federal_platform_map.name: NASA High-End Computing
federal_platform_map.route: NASA-sponsored project / mission request process
federal_platform_map.fit: NASA-aligned Earth/space/engineering computing.
federal_platform_map.boundary: Sponsorship and mission/award review required; not a general open classroom resource.

federal_platform_map.name: NIH AnVIL / Terra ecosystem
federal_platform_map.funding: NIH NHGRI platform funding; cloud usage billed separately
federal_platform_map.route: Project/data authorization plus cloud billing or awarded credits
federal_platform_map.fit: Genomic data-science notebooks, workflows and reproducible biomedical training.
federal_platform_map.boundary: Free platform browsing does not mean free compute/storage/egress. NIH AnVIL differs from Purdue ACCESS Anvil; old credit calls are not current offers.

federal_platform_map.name: CyVerse Discovery Environment / VICE
federal_platform_map.funding: Historical core NSF support; new project funding + subscriptions + Arizona TRIF
federal_platform_map.kind: Managed applications and scientific data platform
federal_platform_map.route: Basic account; confirm institutional Pro or collaboration access
federal_platform_map.fit: Python/R apps, data management and a practical UArizona course/pilot route.
federal_platform_map.boundary: Basic 200 units/year, 5 GB, one job and no sharing/public links. Published UArizona free Pro is state-funded, not universal; GPU and class access need consultation.
federal_platform_map.status: Mixed funding; current published UArizona benefit

federal_platform_map.name: Open Storage Network
federal_platform_map.funding: NSF seed support + participating storage operators
federal_platform_map.route: Separate storage request through ACCESS; provider capacity
federal_platform_map.fit: Large actively used teaching/research datasets and portable object storage.
federal_platform_map.boundary: Documented request range 10–50 TB; not CPU time, backup or archival permanence. Actual size/site capacity needs verification.

federal_platform_map.name: OSDF / Pelican
federal_platform_map.route: Connect existing store or allocated OSN/CC* storage through OSG
federal_platform_map.fit: Deliver data to distributed jobs, notebooks and scientific applications.
federal_platform_map.boundary: Not another storage or compute award. Backing store/access policy required; not for highly regulated/PII/HIPAA data; preservation is separate.
federal_platform_map.parent: OSG data layer; interoperates with OSPool / OSN

federal_platform_map.name: MESA
federal_platform_map.funding: NSF IDSS; project site cites award 2632685
federal_platform_map.route: Published MESA portal/docs; underlying services govern compute
federal_platform_map.fit: Metadata, semantic discovery, reproducible data/agent workflows, Jupyter/R/desktop app layer.
federal_platform_map.boundary: Portal reads the existing CyVerse account/teams/quota; it does not add a second allowance. Selected apps, Save & Exit, per-user Pro/TRIF entitlement, classroom/GPU capacity and support remain to be tested.
federal_platform_map.status: Funded expansion; published portal/tools, readiness untested

federal_platform_map.name: National Data Platform (NDP)
federal_platform_map.route: Public catalog/education activity; consult NDP for class workspace
federal_platform_map.fit: Discoverable compute-ready instructional data, reusable AI activities and capstone content.
federal_platform_map.boundary: Some homepage features are forthcoming. Confirm available workspaces, quota, onboarding and underlying compute rather than equating an IDSS grant with a user allocation.

federal_platform_map.name: Fabric for AI-Driven Science (FabAID)
federal_platform_map.route: Project service endpoints/consultation
federal_platform_map.fit: Storage federation, cache/delivery, transformation, discovery and data-intensive workflows.
federal_platform_map.boundary: Data-service integration complements compute allocations; no universal GPU entitlement, class quota or archival guarantee established.
federal_platform_map.status: Funded deployment; service-specific terms to confirm

federal_platform_map.name: Interactive Discovery Laboratory (iDLab)
federal_platform_map.route: Project consultation; existing site account/allocations as required
federal_platform_map.fit: Browser applications, interactive workspaces and cross-site data/workflow access.
federal_platform_map.boundary: Participating sites retain policies/control. Gateway access is not an extra copy of the sites’ capacity or long-term archives; course readiness must be confirmed.

federal_platform_map.name: BRIDGE National Center / Apache Texera
federal_platform_map.route: Project collaboration or own supported platform deployment
federal_platform_map.fit: Visual/no-code workflows, reproducible social-science/data analyses and shared community models.
federal_platform_map.boundary: May require your own host/cloud/resources and operators. No verified no-cost public compute subscription or guaranteed class capacity.

federal_platform_map.name: National Science Data Fabric (NSDF)
federal_platform_map.route: Project contact; NSF announcement verifies expansion scope
federal_platform_map.fit: Standardized scientific data discovery/access, reproducibility and data/AI workforce development.
federal_platform_map.boundary: Funding/intent verified from NSF announcement; current user-specific access terms, compute quota and production readiness not established in this review.

federal_platform_map.name: Open OnDemand + JupyterHub / BinderHub
federal_platform_map.funding: Open OnDemand federal-supported development; site funds operation
federal_platform_map.route: Use provider-installed portal or deploy on approved compute
federal_platform_map.fit: Notebooks, RStudio, VS Code, remote desktops and visual/science gateways.
federal_platform_map.boundary: Software is not hardware/time allocation. Only Open OnDemand’s funding is evidenced here; no claim that every JupyterHub installation is federally funded. Operators and backing resources remain necessary.

federal_platform_map.name: Pegasus / HTCondor / ACCESS Pegasus
federal_platform_map.kind: Workflow orchestration and job execution products
federal_platform_map.route: Hosted ACCESS Pegasus with active allocation; OSG/PATh tools
federal_platform_map.fit: Portable multi-step pipelines, task sweeps, data staging and transparent execution.
federal_platform_map.boundary: Uses existing allocations/pools; does not create another pool. Software portability is not data preservation or a substitute for operations.

federal_platform_map.name: CILogon / Globus
federal_platform_map.funding: Historical federal development/integration; current operations include subscriptions
federal_platform_map.kind: Identity, authorization and research data movement
federal_platform_map.route: Institution/provider identity configuration and endpoint support
federal_platform_map.fit: Campus login, role-based access, data transfer and cross-site workflow connections.
federal_platform_map.boundary: Basic services may be free while advanced support/sharing costs. Neither supplies a compute/storage allocation; CILogon says operations shifted to subscriptions in 2019.

federal_platform_map.name: Science gateways / SGX3
federal_platform_map.funding: NSF-funded SGX3; substantial operations can be client-funded
federal_platform_map.route: Gateway consultation/community resources; project-specific gateway accounts
federal_platform_map.fit: Usable domain applications and teaching interfaces beyond raw HPC command lines.
federal_platform_map.boundary: Limited funded planning/UX/training differs from paid development/hosting/operations. A gateway catalog is not a universal free app-hosting plan.

federal_platform_map.name: IDSS program
federal_platform_map.kind: Operator grant program, not a compute account
federal_platform_map.route: Institutional proposal / funded project collaboration
federal_platform_map.fit: National data-service development, transition to operations and planning.
federal_platform_map.boundary: Six named 2026 projects have different services/stages; the grant does not award every instructor CPU/GPU hours.

federal_platform_map.name: Campus Cyberinfrastructure (CC*)
federal_platform_map.route: Institutional funding process; actual local award/service rules
federal_platform_map.fit: Campus compute, networking, data storage/digital archives and integration.
federal_platform_map.boundary: Current page has no upcoming due dates and awaits new guidelines. Not an open national classroom account; sharing, operation and stewardship have to be funded.
federal_platform_map.status: Program; current page awaiting new publication

federal_platform_map.name: Major Research Instrumentation (MRI)
federal_platform_map.route: Institutional limited-submission/award process
federal_platform_map.fit: Appropriate shared instrumentation and computing-linked research training.
federal_platform_map.boundary: Current solicitation, instrument eligibility and campus proposal limits matter. A funding route is not a ready device/GPU account; this map does not assert an open submission window.

federal_platform_map.name: State / Regional AI Infrastructure Hubs
federal_platform_map.funding: NSF pays coordination/workforce/education; partners pay infrastructure
federal_platform_map.route: Institution/state/regional consortium; actual award and resource terms
federal_platform_map.fit: Faculty course development, facilitators, shared AI-service coordination and regional scale.
federal_platform_map.boundary: NSF does not acquire/fund the compute infrastructure under this solicitation. Partners must sustain it; no awarded Arizona hub is verified here.

federal_platform_map.name: SCIPE / CyberTraining / ACCESS facilitation
federal_platform_map.route: Existing facilitator/training services or institutional grant pathway
federal_platform_map.fit: Support ownership, instructor onboarding, reusable course materials and train-the-trainer capacity.
federal_platform_map.boundary: Grant programs do not promise staff for every instructor. Current call status and actual support agreements must be checked; college effort is still required.

federal_platform_gaps.title: Many small jobs, not one big notebook
federal_platform_gaps.body: Add OSPool/PATh and checkpointed workflow execution for corpus processing, parameter sweeps and independent model evaluation.

federal_platform_gaps.title: Managed teaching environments
federal_platform_gaps.body: Map CloudBank Classroom, Jetstream2 course images, NRP hubs and eligible CyVerse apps separately from raw GPU allocations.

federal_platform_gaps.title: Inference as an API
federal_platform_gaps.body: NRP-hosted model APIs and requested NAIRR model/software access can support assignments without every student operating a GPU server.

federal_platform_gaps.title: Data-first services
federal_platform_gaps.body: MESA, NDP, FabAID, iDLab, BRIDGE and NSDF supply discovery, metadata, reusable workflows and cross-site access; their grants are not all compute accounts.

federal_platform_gaps.title: Object storage, caches and movement
federal_platform_gaps.body: OSN stores active data; OSDF/Pelican distributes it; Globus moves it. None automatically provides archive permanence or all operating costs.

federal_platform_gaps.title: Systems, networks and specialized hardware
federal_platform_gaps.body: Chameleon, CloudLab and FABRIC support systems/edge/distributed experiments and specialized hardware. Use only when the testbed purpose matches.

federal_platform_gaps.title: Campus delivery and staff funding
federal_platform_gaps.body: Open OnDemand, gateways, identity, orchestration, grant-funded facilitators and college operators make allocations teachable. Compute awards alone do not fund all of them.

federal_platform_gaps.title: Domain facilities and mixed funding
federal_platform_gaps.body: DOE, NASA and NIH add mission-specific routes. CC*/MRI can fund campus capability; AI Hubs and CyVerse/UArizona show why state, subscription and federal support need separate labels.

federal_extension.method: Exa discovery and primary federal/provider documents with targeted direct-live checks. Requested slots are not independently verified source counts. No accounts, allocations, GPU calls, cloud charges, grant submissions or private-project materials were used.
boundaries: Federal development funding is different from current operations or no-cost user access.
ACCESS providers, NRP/Nautilus and OSG/OSPool/OSDF must not be double-counted.
IDSS projects have distinct integration roles and maturity; no generic user quota is implied.
Arizona TRIF is state funding; AI Infrastructure Hubs require partners to finance compute.
Allocated service storage is not automatic archival preservation.

classroom_assessment.title: From federal resources to a classroom service
classroom_assessment.status: Documentation assessment and illustrative capacity model; not an awarded or tested classroom service
classroom_assessment.decision: Use ACCESS for the large CPU and GPU allocation and the classroom pilot. Use campus UITS/AWS only to test CPU components, and free GPU resources to benchmark workloads before piloting. Size the ACCESS request from measured demand; consider CloudBank through ACCESS only if its managed service can meet the confirmed requirements.

representative_courses.name: Data science
representative_courses.work: Python/R data analysis, reproducible notebooks, small-model CPU labs; optional grouped GPU experiment.
representative_courses.fallback: Small CPU datasets and downloadable environment/materials.

representative_courses.name: Library and information science
representative_courses.work: Metadata normalization, collection analysis, public-corpus text processing, reproducible workflow and repository export.
representative_courses.fallback: Local small-record workflow and institution-supported storage; no private patron or grade records on batch resources.

providers.name: CloudBank Classroom
providers.fit: Managed Python/R notebooks and browser IDEs for both courses.
providers.gate: Confirm managed versus broker service, CPU/GPU availability, actual student limits, accounting, course provisioning and exports; previous CPU-only concept is conditional.
providers.limits: No published per-student specification establishes our fit. Fall 2026 GPU pilot is full. General ACCESS route exists; NAIRR Classroom is a separate AI-course route.

providers.name: Jetstream2 through ACCESS
providers.role: ACCESS implementation candidate for CPU + GPU
providers.fit: Own course images, JupyterHub, isolated teaching web/database services and reviewed benchmark workers.
providers.gate: Named operator and backup; CPU/GPU/storage exchange; adequate concurrent quota; tested image upgrade, shutdown, restore and end-of-term export.
providers.limits: Always-on instances dominate credits. Allocation expiry and overdraw can delete resources after thirty days. Storage replication is not independent backup.

providers.name: NRP hosted hub / private hub / API
providers.fit: Notebook canary, grouped GPU demonstrations, model APIs; a primary hub only after class-capacity confirmation.
providers.gate: Confirm hosted/private hub policy, roster and quota, 20 GB home increase from default 5 GB, GPU access and storage/export agreement.
providers.limits: Shared GPU scheduling; ordinary pods have six-hour rules with exceptions. Unused volumes may be purged after six months. APIs are inference products, not training allocations.

providers.name: MESA + CyVerse
providers.fit: MLIS metadata cleanup, collection analysis, reproducibility and portable outputs using public/synthetic records.
providers.gate: Verify each UArizona account’s Pro/TRIF benefit and class approval; rehearse the exact app Save & Exit, restart and export path.
providers.limits: MESA reads existing CyVerse quota. Basic 200 CPU core-hours/year is below this modeled 240 per student (300 with allowance); 5 GB is below modeled 20 GB. Pro is 25,000 units/4 TB/four concurrent jobs per account, not a pooled classroom entitlement.

providers.name: OSPool education program
providers.fit: Independent public-corpus OCR/text analyses and parameter sweeps; teach throughput with a short guest exercise first.
providers.gate: Rehearse a workflow under four hours; retain outputs externally. Arrange full accounts and event/end dates for semester use.
providers.limits: Guest timeout/file loss; full accounts typically expire after event. Interruptible fair share cannot promise synchronous GPU access or assignment completion times. No sensitive/proprietary inputs.

providers.name: PATh Facility
providers.fit: MESA-aligned research ensembles where program eligibility and credits are confirmed.
providers.gate: Ask whether IDSS/MESA is eligible and what work the award can cover; prototype before any full-credit request.
providers.limits: IDSS is not explicitly in the published affiliated-program list. No eligibility or credits verified. Keep required teaching off this route pending confirmation.

providers.name: College + Libraries operations
providers.fit: Support ownership, identity, roster/grade handling, independent backups, durable hosting/databases and archival selection.
providers.gate: Approve owners, operating budget, support coverage, data classification/retention, tested second-host restore and learner exports.
providers.limits: Federal compute does not pay every operating cost or turn working data into preservation. A lab demonstration cannot establish semester service readiness.

scenarios.name: Stopped between sessions
scenarios.boundary: Ideal lower bound for individually stopped/autoscaled 2-vCPU instances. Shared workers have rounding, idle tail, image pulls and orchestration overhead; measure actual billing.

scenarios.name: Student VMs always on
scenarios.boundary: 80 m3.small student instances plus one m3.quad controller, running 24 hours/day for 15 weeks; includes 25% spending allowance.

scenarios.name: Shared hub workers always on
scenarios.boundary: Three m3.2xl workers sized to cover 160 student vCPU and 480 GB RAM, plus one m3.quad controller; placement and hub performance remain untested.

gpu_model.boundary: Eight g3.medium fractional A100 instances shared by groups of five; 120 planned fractional-instance hours is not 120 full-GPU hours. Separate GPU exchange/permission and networking required.

storage_model.boundary: Decimal GB/TB. Working data = 80×20 GB homes + 2×200 GB shared. Independent backup estimate = one working copy + 30 days of 1% changed data/day; excludes compression/deduplication, root disks, images, logs and snapshots. This is not a storage quote or approved retention schedule.

classroom_assessment.allocation_interpretation: Jetstream2-only modeled totals including optional GPU: 38,520 (ideal burst), 518,520 (always-on student VMs), 619,320 (always-on shared workers). CPU and GPU exchanges remain separate. Explore initial ceiling is 200,000 credits (half of 400,000); Discover initial ceiling is 750,000 (half of 1,500,000). A measured small canary can start with Explore. The two always-on models fit within the Discover initial ceiling on paper; approval, actual overhead and provider capacity remain unverified. CloudBank requests use its provider-specific Explore Classroom route, not this VM sizing model.

gates.title: Scope and owners
gates.evidence: Choose real course/syllabus, data classification, operator and backup; fund support and durable storage for the whole term.
gates.stop: No named owner or approved service period.

gates.title: Provider and access
gates.evidence: Confirm approved route, course eligibility, actual roster/login, quotas, images, costs, GPU status and data/expiry terms.

gates.title: Component canary
gates.owner: One instructor + up to ten consenting volunteers
gates.evidence: Run one representative DS assignment and one public-records MLIS workflow; use a fixed image and retain launch, save/restart/export evidence.
gates.stop: Core software or save/export path fails.

gates.title: Capacity rehearsal
gates.evidence: Test approved peak concurrency with provider permission; measure queue/spawn latency, CPU/RAM, storage and actual billed idle time. Suggested p95 login-to-workspace target: five minutes, to negotiate with provider.
gates.stop: Unmeasured or insufficient class capacity; credit/storage forecast exceeds award.

gates.title: Recovery and teach-out
gates.owner: Primary and backup operators + Libraries liaison
gates.evidence: Restore files and service onto a second host; verify cross-student isolation, learner export and grade reconciliation. Proposed RPO 24 hours/RTO one business day require measurement.
gates.stop: No independent restorable backup or viable offline/CPU fallback.

gates.title: Two-course pilot
gates.evidence: 80 illustrative seats; required work CPU-capable. GPU/OSPool/MESA modules only after their own gate passes; collect support time, billing and instructional outcomes.
gates.stop: Unsafe access, recurring capacity failure or no funded support.

gates.title: Retire or renew
gates.when: Decision at least 30 days before expiry (proposed)
gates.evidence: Export students/grades, reconcile submissions, deposit approved public outputs with Libraries; confirm next-term project/renewal route and verify deletion.
gates.stop: Assuming automatic education extension or treating grace periods as service funding.

classroom_assessment.operations_model: Available cash budget is zero. Work needing paid support, storage, hosting, development or recovery must have a confirmed eligible EduCloud grant and allowable work package before spending. ACCESS is CPU/GPU resource allocation, not payroll. No grant award is asserted. Existing campus test access and free GPU resources must stay within their authorized no-purchase scope. Greg has ten hours/week total. Separate potential TA effort is 102 hours and additional course-lead effort 70 hours across the modeled term; no course-lead salary. No college sponsor/finance role. Distinct backup/support is unfilled until confirmed.
classroom_assessment.degree_expansion: The first canary covers DS and MLIS. Notebook-compatible MS/BS Information Science and PhD projects can reuse the route after workload review. ETS and Information Science and Arts need public-data/browser workflows and durable exhibit hosting. Game Design/Development require a separate engine, graphics, licensing and desktop-access assessment; this notebook pilot does not establish Unreal/Unity or Windows support. Cyber degrees remain excluded.
classroom_assessment.method: 16 discovery queries requested 78 result slots; these are discovery counts, not independent evidence counts. Twenty new primary-source ledger records plus reused program/provider records support a qualitative fit assessment. Public documentation was read, with saved extracts and targeted HTTP access checks. No signed-in entitlement, actual compute workload, model API, cloud billing, allocation request, provider message or grant submission was executed. Current user-directed route: campus UITS/AWS is for CPU component testing only; free GPU benchmarks precede piloting; ACCESS covers the planned CPU and GPU classroom allocation. Existing capacity models remain illustrative.

classroom50_assessment.status: Workable successor to assess; no signed-in canary or adoption completed
classroom50_assessment.verdict: Classroom 50 is a workable successor for assignment management. It is not something we own, and it does not increase GitHub Codespaces free compute.

Self-hosting still needs authentication/proxy review, updates and recovery. No UArizona deployment or funded operator is assumed.
